prompt: Which of the following best describes a one-way function?

options.label: Easy to compute in one direction, hard to invert
A function with no inverse at all
A function that always returns the same output

explanation: A one-way function must still have an inverse in principle — "no inverse at all" would make it uninvertible even for the person who created it, which breaks schemes like public-key encryption that rely on the owner being able to reverse it with a secret key.
